summary: Crash when modifying age property of a pitcher crop
description: The game crashes if the age property of a pitcher crop s top half is set too high. This can be done with a debug stick by a creative user. Steps to reproduce 1. Place farmland 2. Place a pitcher pod on the farmland 3. Fertilize the pitcher crop with bonemeal until it is two blocks high 4. Select the age property with the debug stick 5. Increment the age until the game crashes
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
2. Place farmland at your current location.
3. Place a pitcher pod on top of the farmland.
4. Use bonemeal to fertilize the pitcher crop until it grows two blocks high.
5. Select the age property of the top half of the pitcher crop using a debug stick.
6. Increment the age value with the debug stick until the game crashes.
7. Note the coordinates and take a screenshot for documentation.
Observed Behavior: The game crashes if the age property of a pitcher crop's top half is set too high using a debug stick, which can be done by creative users. To reproduce this issue, first place farmland and then plant a pitcher pod on it. Next, use bonemeal to fertilize the pitcher crop until it grows to two blocks high. Once the crop has reached this height, select its age property with the debug stick and increment the value until the game crashes. This behavior indicates that setting an excessively high age value for the top half of a pitcher crop results in a critical error, leading to a complete crash of the Minecraft environment.
Expected Behavior: When following the steps to modify the age property of a pitcher crop with a debug stick, the game should not crash. Instead, incrementing the age property beyond typical values should simply cap at the maximum allowed value for the pitcher crop's growth stages without causing any instability or crashes. The crop should remain in its final mature state without affecting game stability.
